claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch now because current-release evidence is sufficient and the known vendor-screening subgroup weakness can be handled through current-release documentation/disclosure rather than requiring resolution or approved risk acceptance before launch.
decision_criteria: Use `compliant` only if admissible evidence shows current-release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material subgroup weakness is either disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.

Use `suspicious` when the evidence plausibly supports readiness in part but a required support link remains missing; that is the case here because aggregate readiness exists but proof of required disclosure/mitigation is absent.

The existence of aggregate pass and no severity-one incidents is relevant but not sufficient to satisfy the model-card certification policy when a material segment weakness remains unresolved in the record.
A prior approval and informal monitoring note may inform context, but under the policy they cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed risk acceptance.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release model card or equivalent release documentation showing the vendor-screening subgroup limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide any approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record, if certification is being justified without disclosure-based closure.
Provide the current-release certification packet or sign-off artifact tying the cited evaluation results to the released documentation.
specific_concerns: The policy permits certification only if current-release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is disclosed or covered by approved mitigation; the record includes the policy note but not the actual current release documentation showing that disclosure.
The supply-chain vendor-screening slice is below the warning threshold for a named launch use case, which is affirmative evidence of a current material weakness.
The release-thread monitoring comment shows awareness only; the evidence expressly says no reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language is attached.
Prior approval is explicitly stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot carry the present certification decision.
unsupported_claims: That launch may proceed now, because no admissible evidence shows the required current model-card disclosure has actually been included.

That certification is already defensible on a documentation-dependent basis, because the packet describes what the strongest packet should say rather than proving those materials exist in the current release record.
Any implication that informal post-launch monitoring functions as approved mitigation or risk acceptance.
